mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such tightening episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median market return at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during these episodes (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflationary environment, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during these episodes (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 while the unemployment rate is below 5% signals an overheating labor market, which triggers preemptive monetary tightening and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with strong payroll growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in these instances (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which drags on construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes or the average return is not statistically below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in Real Personal Income (implied by GDPC1 and RSAFS dynamics) exceeding 4% combined with a flat or declining unemployment rate signals robust household demand without labor market overheating, which supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 4% AND UNRATE flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in these episodes (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is negative.
